ai.subject: Medicine
ai.summary: Thyroid disease encompasses disorders of hormone production, ranging from hypo- to hyperthyroidism. Clinical reasoning focuses on symptom patterns, laboratory clues, and context such as infections or medications. Management balances treating the underlying cause with hormone replacement or suppression.

sections.p: Thyroid disease refers to any dysfunction of the thyroid gland, affecting hormone synthesis or release. Diagnosis integrates clinical features, serum TSH, free T4/T3, and antibodies when indicated.
b: TSH is the primary screening test; abnormal values trigger further testing.

t.b: High TSH suggests hypothyroidism; low TSH indicates hyperthyroidism.
Low in hypothyroidism; high in hyperthyroidism.
Positive in Hashimoto or Graves disease.

sections.p: Severity is graded by symptom burden and biochemical extremes. Myxoedema coma and thyrotoxic crisis are life‑threatening stages requiring urgent care.
b: Hyperthyroid: mild (TSH <0.1, T4 normal), moderate (TSH <0.1, T4 high), severe (thyroid storm).

sections.p: Autoimmune disease dominates. In low‑resource settings, iodine deficiency, infections, and herbal remedies also play major roles.
b: Infections: TB, HIV, malaria can trigger thyroiditis.

sections.p: Symptoms reflect hormone excess or deficiency, often subtle. Contextual clues (e.g., recent infection, medication) guide differential.
b: Hypothyroid: fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation.
Hyperthyroid: palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, weight loss.

sections.p: Lab tests answer specific questions; imaging is reserved for nodules or structural disease.

t.b: Low in hypothyroid; high in hyperthyroid.

sections.p: Certain presentations signal imminent danger and require immediate intervention.
b: Myxoedema coma: hypothermia, hypotension, altered consciousness.

sections.p: Treat the underlying cause first, then adjust hormone levels. Drug choice reflects safety, availability, and interaction profile.
b: Antithyroid drugs (propylthiouracil, methimazole) for Graves; avoid in pregnancy.
Levothyroxine for hypothyroidism; start low, titrate.

sections.p: Regular monitoring of hormone levels and symptom review prevent overtreatment or relapse. Public health iodine supplementation reduces deficiency.
Many conditions mimic thyroid dysfunction; distinguishing features are key.
Certain lab values may be falsely normal or abnormal due to interference or disease state.
b: TSH can be suppressed in non‑thyroidal illness; interpret with clinical context.
